newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures mostly end off on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures mostly end off on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Monday in a moderate session, with front months weighed down by forecasts for much milder Midwest and East Coast weather this week, industry sources said.
February skidded 18.7 cents to close at $3.07 per million British thermal units after briefly dipping below $3 early. March settled 8.5 cents lower at $2.774.

"The weather is moderating, cash was down big and the market sold off, but they brought it down to a new level and then didn't know what to do with it," said one East Coast trader, adding sentiment now seemed more bearish.
Cratering cash prices, down about 30 percent since Thursday, helped undermine paper, and most agreed without a long bout of Arctic cold, the bulls could be on the defensive for a while.
"If we don't get winter to take some of this gas away, the spreads and outrights are going to collapse again," said a Midwest trader, referring to flatter front-to-back spread relationships recently.
Temperatures in the eastern half of the nation are expected to moderate this week, then turn colder by the weekend, at least across northern tier states.

Technically, traders pegged psychological support in February at $3, with better buying likely at the Dec 31 low of $2.613. Resistance was seen at $3.33, $3.64 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area. The spot contract expires next Monday.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices tumbled another 60 cents Monday to the $3.20s. Midcontinent pipes skidded a similar amount to the $2.90s. Gas at the New York city gate plunged $2 to the low-$4 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 3.3 cents to $2.362. NYMEX said an estimated 37,927 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 45,266.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Monday.

On the KCBT, February closed 17 cents lower at $2.93, while deferreds finished down by one to seven cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.7 cents to 14 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 160 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 405.
